subject: Urgent: Suncrest throughput & p99 spike after v2.3 quant pack — exec review requested
messages:
From: Olivia Hart <olivia.hart@suncrest.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-28T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden p99/throughput regression after v2.3 quant profile deployment

Hi Jonas / Neha —

We pushed the v2.3 model with the new quantization profile last night (per the rollout plan). Since ~02:30 UTC this morning we've seen a sustained p99 latency increase (~650ms → ~1.4s) and several 503 spikes during bursts. Throughput at our expected concurrency dropped ~25% compared to the v2.2 baseline. Attached are traces and the quant profile you shipped.

This is customer-impacting: our ingestion pipeline is backing up and customers in EMEA are reporting timeouts. Please treat this as a Sev-2 with executive visibility — Suncrest leadership is already on the thread. We need immediate mitigation steps and a timeline for root cause and rollback if required.

Olivia
VP of Platform Engineering
Suncrest Analytics

Attachments: suncrest_p99_traces.zip, v2.3-quant-profile.json
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Hart <olivia.hart@suncrest.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-28T15:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99/throughput regression after v2.3 quant profile deployment

Hi Olivia —

Really sorry about the disruption and thank you for sending the artifacts. We're taking this seriously. Initial ack from our side:
- I've opened an internal incident and assigned neha and dylan to Triage.
- Can you confirm whether you used the exact v2.3 quant bundle we provided yesterday (filename v2.3-quant-profile.json) or if you modified any thresholds?
- We'll start with an immediate traffic hatch: if you want us to, we can flip your production routing to v2.2 (our prior stable). Would you prefer a temporary rollback now or let us attempt a quick mitigation (batch size caps / rebalancing) first?

I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes.

— Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-28T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99/throughput regression after v2.3 quant profile deployment

Jonas / Dylan —

Quick notes from triage (pulling metrics and runtime snapshots now):
- Canary nodes show increased kernel churn and slower KV-cache hit rate under the same request mix after applying the v2.3 quant pack.
- CPU on the scheduler hosts spiked during longer sequences; token times increased ~2x for sequences >256 tokens.
- The quant packing changed per-layer packing heuristics; it looks like some attention kernels are now running on the fallback slower path on NVIDIA A10s in Suncrest's cluster.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Recommend rolling Suncrest back to v2.2 for production (safe, fast).
2) Concurrently run a diagnostic canary with v2.3 but force the old quant packing to see if the quant heuristics cause the hit.
3) Provide a patch to the kernel selector to avoid the fallback path for affected attention shapes; this will take ~24–48 hours to test and stage.

I'll attach the canary_metrics_1129.csv once the aggregator finishes (will drop into the Drive link).

— Neha
Senior ML Infra Engineer
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-29T08:43:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Sudden p99/throughput regression — need exec sign-off for rollback

Marissa — forwarding the Suncrest thread. TL;DR: v2.3 quant pack caused p99 and throughput regressions on their A10 clusters. Neha recommends immediate rollback to v2.2 for production, plus a canary with quant heuristics disabled to isolate root cause.

If we proceed with rollback now we need exec OK for:
- Authorization to change Suncrest routing (we have the runbook but this is a customer-managed cluster with Redwood-managed model versions).
- Temporary credit for the incident (Suncrest is asking for remediation).

On the customer side, leadership is watching and procurement is copied. Rolling back reduces short-term risk but we should be transparent about the timeline for a permanent fix.

Date: 2026-11-30T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99/throughput regression after v2.3 quant profile deployment

Olivia —

Thank you for the quick escalation and for the artifacts. First, sincere apologies for the impact to Suncrest customers. We take regressions seriously and want to resolve this with urgency. Approved immediate steps:

1) We will revert your production traffic to model v2.2 within the next 20 minutes. This is an operational rollback only; no schema or prompt changes required.
2) We'll run a gated canary for v2.3 with quant heuristics disabled while we investigate. Neha's team will own the diagnostics.
3) Redwood will open a formal post-incident review with Suncrest and provide a mitigation credit for the service interruption; we'll follow-up with our finance/sales team for the exact credit size (we'll target a customer-impact credit within 72 hours).

We expect to have a technical assessment (kernel selector root-cause hypothesis and timeline for a fix) within 48 hours. I'll join the customer call if you want an executive presence — propose a 30-minute sync at 17:00 UTC today to align on rollback and follow-ups.

Again, apologies and thank you for the patience. We'll aim to make this right.

— Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
